phase2_claim_boundary: The roadmap identifies technically plausible Phase 2 extensions. It does not claim that scale-up, hardware advantage, real-world deployment, or production safety has already been demonstrated.

priorities.objective: Replace the compact Phase 1 proxy backbone with a larger pretrained VLA-style representation.
priorities.phase1_gap_addressed: Phase 1 used a compact synthetic shared VLA proxy.

priorities.objective: Connect the VLA shared latent representation directly to classical PPO and hybrid PQC policy heads.
priorities.phase1_gap_addressed: Sprint 4 policies operated on compact environment state rather than the Sprint 1 shared latent.

priorities.objective: Evaluate TT/MPS compression on larger VLA projection, fusion, and attention-related matrices.
priorities.phase1_gap_addressed: Phase 1 tensor-network experiments were limited to the compact pilot architecture.

priorities.objective: Move from synthetic proxy environments to realistic driving and robotics benchmarks.
priorities.phase1_gap_addressed: Phase 1 validation used synthetic proxy environments.

priorities.objective: Evaluate safety filters when both policy and safety layer receive estimated or noisy state.
priorities.phase1_gap_addressed: Phase 1 perception-perturbation studies allowed the safety layer access to true simulator state.

priorities.objective: Measure end-to-end latency, memory, and safety-filter overhead on embedded hardware.
priorities.phase1_gap_addressed: Phase 1 compact CPU latency does not represent full-scale VLA deployment latency.

priorities.objective: Extend PQC studies to larger circuits, noisy simulation, and hardware execution where available.
priorities.phase1_gap_addressed: Phase 1 used a small simulated PQC and did not demonstrate quantum advantage.

priorities.objective: Increase statistical strength and broaden evaluation.
priorities.phase1_gap_addressed: Phase 1 used three principal seeds and compact evaluation settings.
